description: The THROUGH range's [ IN alphabet-name-1 ] phrase - ISO 14.9.13.2's range-expression (EVALUATE WHEN) and 13.18.63.2 formats 3 and 5 (the condition-name VALUE clause), governed together by 14.7.8 GR2 ('When the IN alphabet-name phrase is specified, the collating sequence used for range evaluation is the collating sequence defined by that alphabet'). Not the SPECIAL-NAMES ALPHABET clause's own `literal-1 THROUGH literal-2` character range, which COBOL-85 already has (§1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4d) and which no edition gates. A COBOL-2002 addition. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85's EVALUATE and VALUE formats carry a bare THROUGH pair ordered by comparison - §1985:VI.6.13.4 GR1g, 'the range of values includes all permissible values of the selection subject that are greater than or equal to the first operand and less than or equal to the second operand according to the rules for comparison', §1985:VI.6.13.3 SR4, 'Two operands connected by a THROUGH phrase must be of the same class', and §1985:VI.5.15.5 GR2, 'Wherever the THRU phrase is used, literal-2 must be less than literal-3'; §2002:14.6.7 ('This specification applies to THROUGH phrases specified in the VALUE clause and the EVALUATE statement') adds 'When the IN alphabet-name phrase is specified, the collating sequence used for range evaluation is the collating sequence defined by that alphabet', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 136: 'THROUGH phrase in VALUE clause and EVALUATE statement. A collating sequence can be identified in the THROUGH phrase for use in determining a range of values.' §2014:14.7.7 carries the same sentence, so 2014 = 2023. Gated at the ONE resolver both formats reach, SpecialNamesBinder.TryResolveRangeAlphabet (kb/Work PB1015), because the phrase is decided by SYMBOL, not by position: IN is an optional word (kb/Work PB983) and an EVALUATE identifier-4 IN word parses as a qualification until the binder peels it (PB843), so no parse-arm recognition can see every spelling. Fires only once the word IS an alphabet-name (a word naming no alphabet is not the phrase).
display: the THROUGH range's IN alphabet-name phrase
vcr: THROUGH range IN alphabet-name-1 phrase (COBOL-2002, quoted: §2002:14.6.7 and §2002:F.2 item 136 against §1985:VI.6.13.4 GR1g); kb/Work PB1015; VCR row 7.22
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMRNGIN.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
SPECIAL-NAMES.
    ALPHABET AL IS NATIVE.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 WS-C PIC X VALUE "C".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    EVALUATE WS-C
        WHEN "A" THRU "M" IN AL DISPLAY "IN"
        WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "OUT"
    END-EVALUATE.
    STOP RUN.
